modules.title: Window Functions
modules.goal: Compute rankings, running totals and row comparisons without collapsing rows.

topics.title: Window Function Basics
topics.simple: Window functions har row ke saath related rows par calculate karte hain.
topics.pro: A window function computes across a set of related rows while keeping every row in the result.
points: The result can be ranked or accumulated.

example.sql: SELECT name, marks, SUM(marks) OVER () AS total FROM students;
example.output: Every student plus the overall total.

topics.title: OVER Clause
topics.simple: OVER window ka shape batata hai.
topics.pro: OVER introduces the window specification and can include PARTITION BY, ORDER BY and a frame.
points: Empty OVER means the whole result.

example.sql: SELECT name, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY marks DESC) AS rank FROM students;

topics.title: PARTITION BY
topics.simple: PARTITION BY rows ko independent groups me todta hai.
topics.pro: PARTITION BY restarts the window calculation for each group without removing rows.
points: It is like GROUP BY without collapsing.
Missing it makes one global window.

example.sql: SELECT course_id, student_id, COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY course_id) AS enrolled FROM enrollments;
example.output: Enrollment count repeated per course row.

topics.title: ORDER BY in Windows
topics.simple: Window ORDER BY calculation ka sequence set karta hai.
topics.pro: ORDER BY inside OVER defines the row order used by ranking, lag and running calculations.
points: It is separate from final ORDER BY.

example.sql: SELECT name, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY marks DESC, id ASC) AS rn FROM students;

topics.title: ROW_NUMBER
topics.simple: ROW_NUMBER har row ko unique sequence number deta hai.
topics.pro: ROW_NUMBER assigns 1, 2, 3 and so on in window order, even when values tie.
points: Ties are broken arbitrarily unless the ORDER BY is total.
It is useful for top-N per group.

example.sql: SELECT name, marks, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY marks DESC, id ASC) AS rn FROM students;

topics.title: RANK
topics.simple: RANK ties ko same rank deta hai aur gaps chhodta hai.
topics.pro: RANK assigns the same rank to tied rows and leaves gaps after a tie.

example.sql: SELECT name, marks, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY marks DESC) AS rank FROM students;
example.output: Ties share a rank, then gaps.

topics.title: DENSE_RANK
topics.simple: DENSE_RANK ties ko same rank deta hai bina gaps ke.
topics.pro: DENSE_RANK gives tied rows the same rank but does not leave gaps.
points: It is useful for grade bands.

example.sql: SELECT name, marks, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY marks DESC) AS rank FROM students;

topics.title: NTILE
topics.simple: NTILE rows ko N buckets me baantta hai.
topics.pro: NTILE(n) divides the ordered rows into n buckets, putting larger buckets first when the rows do not divide evenly.
points: Sizes differ by at most one.

example.sql: SELECT name, marks, NTILE(4) OVER (ORDER BY marks DESC) AS quartile FROM students;

topics.title: LAG
topics.simple: LAG previous row ki value deta hai.
topics.pro: LAG returns a value from an earlier row in the window, with an optional offset and default.

example.sql: SELECT name, marks, LAG(marks) OVER (ORDER BY id) AS previous FROM students;

topics.title: LEAD
topics.simple: LEAD next row ki value deta hai.
topics.pro: LEAD returns a value from a later row in the window, with an optional offset and default.
points: It is useful for next-step analysis.

example.sql: SELECT name, marks, LEAD(marks) OVER (ORDER BY id) AS next_mark FROM students;

topics.title: FIRST_VALUE
topics.simple: FIRST_VALUE window ke first row ki value deta hai.
topics.pro: FIRST_VALUE returns the value from the first row of the window frame, which is often the group leader.

example.sql: SELECT name, marks, FIRST_VALUE(name) OVER (ORDER BY marks DESC) AS top_name FROM students;
example.output: Every row shows the top name.

topics.title: LAST_VALUE
topics.simple: LAST_VALUE frame ke last row ki value deta hai.
topics.pro: LAST_VALUE returns the last row of the current frame; with the default frame that is often the current row, so an explicit full frame is usually needed.
points: The default frame ends at the current row.
Use UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING for the true last row.

example.sql: SELECT name, LAST_VALUE(name) OVER (ORDER BY marks DESC ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING) AS last_name FROM students;
example.output: Every row shows the lowest-ranked name.

topics.title: Running Totals
topics.simple: Running total current row tak accumulate karta hai.
topics.pro: A running total uses SUM with an ordered frame from the start of the partition to the current row.

example.sql: SELECT id, marks, SUM(marks) OVER (ORDER BY id ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running FROM students;

topics.title: Moving Averages
topics.simple: Moving average nearby rows ka average deta hai.
topics.pro: A moving average uses a bounded frame such as two preceding rows through the current row.

example.sql: SELECT id, marks, AVG(marks) OVER (ORDER BY id ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS moving_avg FROM students;

topics.title: Window Frames
topics.simple: Frame batata hai kaunse rows current calculation me shaamil hain.
topics.pro: A frame clause defines the start and end boundaries inside the partition, using ROWS, RANGE or GROUPS.

example.sql: SELECT id, marks, SUM(marks) OVER (ORDER BY id ROWS BETWEEN 1 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING) AS nearby FROM students;

topics.title: ROWS vs RANGE
topics.simple: ROWS physical rows ginata hai; RANGE value ranges par kaam karta hai.
topics.pro: ROWS addresses physical row offsets, while RANGE groups peers with equal ORDER BY values before applying the boundary.
points: ROWS is precise for row counts.

example.sql: SELECT marks, SUM(marks) OVER (ORDER BY marks RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS cumulative FROM students;
example.output: Peers receive the same cumulative value.

topics.title: Named Windows
topics.simple: WINDOW clause ek window ko naam dekar reuse karta hai.
topics.pro: A named window defined in WINDOW can be reused by several window functions in the same query.

example.sql: SELECT course_id, student_id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER w AS rn FROM enrollments WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY course_id ORDER BY student_id);

topics.title: Window vs GROUP BY
topics.simple: GROUP BY rows collapse karta hai; window rows preserve karta hai.
topics.pro: GROUP BY returns one row per group, while a window function returns one row per input row with the group calculation attached.

example.sql: SELECT course_id, COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY course_id) AS enrolled FROM enrollments;
example.output: Every enrollment row with its course count.

topics.title: Window Performance
topics.simple: Window functions sort aur memory use kar sakte hain.
topics.pro: Window execution often requires sorting by partition and order keys, so matching indexes and narrow frames reduce the cost.
points: Index the partition and order keys.

example.sql: EXPLAIN SELECT name, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY marks DESC) FROM students;
example.output: A plan with a WindowAgg and Sort.

topics.title: Practical Window Report
topics.simple: Windows se ranking, running totals aur per-group top N banao.
topics.pro: A practical report combines a partition, an order, a ranking function and an outer filter on the rank alias.
points: Rank in a CTE or subquery.

example.sql: WITH ranked AS (SELECT course_id, student_id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY course_id ORDER BY student_id) AS rn FROM enrollments) SELECT * FROM ranked WHERE rn <= 3;
example.output: The first three students per course.

interview.q: Module 15 · Explain Window Function Basics in a production query.
interview.answer: A window function computes across a set of related rows while keeping every row in the result. Key rules: OVER defines the window. Rows are not collapsed. The result can be ranked or accumulated.

interview.q: Module 15 · Explain OVER Clause in a production query.
interview.answer: OVER introduces the window specification and can include PARTITION BY, ORDER BY and a frame. Key rules: OVER is mandatory. Empty OVER means the whole result. It follows the function call.

interview.q: Module 15 · Explain PARTITION BY in a production query.
interview.answer: PARTITION BY restarts the window calculation for each group without removing rows. Key rules: Each partition is independent. It is like GROUP BY without collapsing. Missing it makes one global window.

interview.q: Module 15 · Explain ORDER BY in Windows in a production query.
interview.answer: ORDER BY inside OVER defines the row order used by ranking, lag and running calculations. Key rules: It is separate from final ORDER BY. It controls the frame direction. Ties need a deterministic key.

interview.q: Module 15 · Explain ROW_NUMBER in a production query.
interview.answer: ROW_NUMBER assigns 1, 2, 3 and so on in window order, even when values tie. Key rules: It is unique per partition. Ties are broken arbitrarily unless the ORDER BY is total. It is useful for top-N per group.

interview.q: Module 15 · Explain RANK in a production query.
interview.answer: RANK assigns the same rank to tied rows and leaves gaps after a tie. Key rules: Ties share a rank. Gaps appear after ties. It follows competition ranking.

interview.q: Module 15 · Explain DENSE_RANK in a production query.
interview.answer: DENSE_RANK gives tied rows the same rank but does not leave gaps. Key rules: Ties share a rank. No gaps appear. It is useful for grade bands.

interview.q: Module 15 · Explain NTILE in a production query.
interview.answer: NTILE(n) divides the ordered rows into n buckets, putting larger buckets first when the rows do not divide evenly. Key rules: Buckets are numbered 1 to n. Rows are ordered first. Sizes differ by at most one.

interview.q: Module 15 · Explain LAG in a production query.
interview.answer: LAG returns a value from an earlier row in the window, with an optional offset and default. Key rules: Offset defaults to 1. The default is NULL. It is useful for deltas.

interview.q: Module 15 · Explain LEAD in a production query.
interview.answer: LEAD returns a value from a later row in the window, with an optional offset and default. Key rules: Offset defaults to 1. The last row gets NULL. It is useful for next-step analysis.

interview.q: Module 15 · Explain FIRST_VALUE in a production query.
interview.answer: FIRST_VALUE returns the value from the first row of the window frame, which is often the group leader. Key rules: It respects the frame. It can be partitioned. It is useful for comparisons.

interview.q: Module 15 · Explain LAST_VALUE in a production query.
interview.answer: LAST_VALUE returns the last row of the current frame; with the default frame that is often the current row, so an explicit full frame is usually needed. Key rules: The default frame ends at the current row. Use UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING for the true last row. It respects PARTITION BY.

interview.q: Module 15 · Explain Running Totals in a production query.
interview.answer: A running total uses SUM with an ordered frame from the start of the partition to the current row. Key rules: Order the rows. Use an unbounded preceding frame. Partition to restart per group.

interview.q: Module 15 · Explain Moving Averages in a production query.
interview.answer: A moving average uses a bounded frame such as two preceding rows through the current row. Key rules: Choose the frame width. Order by a stable key. Partition when averages restart.

interview.q: Module 15 · Explain Window Frames in a production query.
interview.answer: A frame clause defines the start and end boundaries inside the partition, using ROWS, RANGE or GROUPS. Key rules: Frames apply to ordered windows. ROWS counts physical rows. RANGE counts value ranges.

interview.q: Module 15 · Explain ROWS vs RANGE in a production query.
interview.answer: ROWS addresses physical row offsets, while RANGE groups peers with equal ORDER BY values before applying the boundary. Key rules: ROWS is precise for row counts. RANGE includes peer rows. Duplicates behave differently.

interview.q: Module 15 · Explain Named Windows in a production query.
interview.answer: A named window defined in WINDOW can be reused by several window functions in the same query. Key rules: Define it after FROM. Reference it in OVER. It reduces repetition.

interview.q: Module 15 · Explain Window vs GROUP BY in a production query.
interview.answer: GROUP BY returns one row per group, while a window function returns one row per input row with the group calculation attached. Key rules: GROUP BY changes the grain. Windows preserve the grain. Both can use partitions.

interview.q: Module 15 · Explain Window Performance in a production query.
interview.answer: Window execution often requires sorting by partition and order keys, so matching indexes and narrow frames reduce the cost. Key rules: Index the partition and order keys. Narrow the frame when possible. Read EXPLAIN for WindowAgg.

interview.q: Module 15 · Explain Practical Window Report in a production query.
interview.answer: A practical report combines a partition, an order, a ranking function and an outer filter on the rank alias. Key rules: Rank in a CTE or subquery. Filter the rank outside. State the result grain.

logic.q: Module 15 · Why does Window Function Basics matter?
logic.answer: A window function computes across a set of related rows while keeping every row in the result. OVER defines the window. Rows are not collapsed. The result can be ranked or accumulated.

logic.q: Module 15 · Why does OVER Clause matter?
logic.answer: OVER introduces the window specification and can include PARTITION BY, ORDER BY and a frame. OVER is mandatory. Empty OVER means the whole result. It follows the function call.

logic.q: Module 15 · Why does PARTITION BY matter?
logic.answer: PARTITION BY restarts the window calculation for each group without removing rows. Each partition is independent. It is like GROUP BY without collapsing. Missing it makes one global window.

logic.q: Module 15 · Why does ORDER BY in Windows matter?
logic.answer: ORDER BY inside OVER defines the row order used by ranking, lag and running calculations. It is separate from final ORDER BY. It controls the frame direction. Ties need a deterministic key.
ROW_NUMBER assigns 1, 2, 3 and so on in window order, even when values tie. It is unique per partition. Ties are broken arbitrarily unless the ORDER BY is total. It is useful for top-N per group.
RANK assigns the same rank to tied rows and leaves gaps after a tie. Ties share a rank. Gaps appear after ties. It follows competition ranking.
DENSE_RANK gives tied rows the same rank but does not leave gaps. Ties share a rank. No gaps appear. It is useful for grade bands.
NTILE(n) divides the ordered rows into n buckets, putting larger buckets first when the rows do not divide evenly. Buckets are numbered 1 to n. Rows are ordered first. Sizes differ by at most one.
LAG returns a value from an earlier row in the window, with an optional offset and default. Offset defaults to 1. The default is NULL. It is useful for deltas.
LEAD returns a value from a later row in the window, with an optional offset and default. Offset defaults to 1. The last row gets NULL. It is useful for next-step analysis.
FIRST_VALUE returns the value from the first row of the window frame, which is often the group leader. It respects the frame. It can be partitioned. It is useful for comparisons.

LAST_VALUE returns the last row of the current frame; with the default frame that is often the current row, so an explicit full frame is usually needed. The default frame ends at the current row. Use UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING for the true last row. It respects PARTITION BY.

logic.q: Module 15 · Why does Running Totals matter?
logic.answer: A running total uses SUM with an ordered frame from the start of the partition to the current row. Order the rows. Use an unbounded preceding frame. Partition to restart per group.

logic.q: Module 15 · Why does Moving Averages matter?
logic.answer: A moving average uses a bounded frame such as two preceding rows through the current row. Choose the frame width. Order by a stable key. Partition when averages restart.

logic.q: Module 15 · Why does Window Frames matter?
logic.answer: A frame clause defines the start and end boundaries inside the partition, using ROWS, RANGE or GROUPS. Frames apply to ordered windows. ROWS counts physical rows. RANGE counts value ranges.

debug.title: Window in WHERE
debug.broken: SELECT name FROM students WHERE ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY marks DESC) = 1;
debug.fix: WITH ranked AS (SELECT name, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY marks DESC) AS rn FROM students) SELECT name FROM ranked WHERE rn = 1;
debug.error: window functions are not allowed in WHERE

debug.title: Missing OVER
debug.fix: SELECT name, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY marks DESC) FROM students;
debug.error: window function row_number requires an OVER clause

debug.title: LAST_VALUE default frame
debug.broken: SELECT name, LAST_VALUE(name) OVER (ORDER BY marks DESC) AS last_name FROM students;
debug.fix: SELECT name, LAST_VALUE(name) OVER (ORDER BY marks DESC ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING) AS last_name FROM students;
debug.error: LAST_VALUE returns the current row with the default frame

debug.title: Reversed frame
debug.broken: SELECT name, SUM(marks) OVER (ORDER BY id ROWS BETWEEN 1 FOLLOWING AND 1 PRECEDING) FROM students;
debug.fix: SELECT name, SUM(marks) OVER (ORDER BY id ROWS BETWEEN 1 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING) FROM students;
debug.error: frame starting boundary cannot follow ending boundary

debug.title: Window in GROUP BY
debug.broken: SELECT name, ROW_NUMBER() OVER () FROM students GROUP BY name;
debug.fix: SELECT name, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY name) FROM students;
debug.error: window functions are not allowed in GROUP BY

debug.title: Rank alias in WHERE
debug.broken: SELECT name, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY marks DESC) AS rn FROM students WHERE rn = 1;
debug.fix: WITH ranked AS (SELECT name, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY marks DESC) AS rn FROM students) SELECT name FROM ranked WHERE rn = 1;

debug.title: Missing partition
debug.broken: SELECT course_id, student_id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY student_id) AS rn FROM enrollments;
debug.fix: SELECT course_id, student_id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY course_id ORDER BY student_id) AS rn FROM enrollments;

debug.title: Nested window
debug.broken: SELECT ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY RANK() OVER (ORDER BY marks DESC)) FROM students;
debug.fix: WITH ranked AS (SELECT name, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY marks DESC) AS r FROM students) SELECT ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY r) FROM ranked;

debug.title: Missing column
debug.broken: SELECT student_id, COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY course_id) FROM students;
debug.fix: SELECT student_id, COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY course_id) FROM enrollments;

debug.title: Incomplete frame
debug.broken: SELECT name, SUM(marks) OVER (ORDER BY id ROWS BETWEEN 1 PRECEDING) FROM students;
debug.fix: SELECT name, SUM(marks) OVER (ORDER BY id ROWS BETWEEN 1 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) FROM students;
